[[File:Great icosidodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great icosidodecahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great icosidodecahedron''' is a [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>54</sub>. It has 32 faces (20 [[Triangle|triangles]] and 12 [[Pentagram|pentagrams]]), 60 edges, and 30 vertices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathconsult.ch/static/unipoly/54.html|title=54: great icosidodecahedron|last=Maeder|first=Roman|date=|website=MathConsult|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> It is given a [[Schläfli symbol]] r{3,{{frac|5|2}}}. It is the [[Rectification (geometry)|rectification]] of the [[great stellated dodecahedron]] and the [[great icosahedron]]. It was discovered independently by {{harvs|txt|last=Hess|authorlink=Edmund Hess|year=1878}}, {{harvs|txt|last=Badoureau|year=1881}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Pitsch|year=1882}}.

== Related polyhedra ==
The figure is a [[rectification (geometry)|rectification]] of the [[great icosahedron]] or the [[great stellated dodecahedron]], much as the (small) [[icosidodecahedron]] is related to the (small) [[icosahedron]] and (small) [[dodecahedron]], and the [[cuboctahedron]] to the [[cube]] and [[octahedron]].

It shares its [[vertex arrangement]] with the icosidodecahedron, which is its [[convex hull]]. Unlike the [[great icosahedron]] and [[great dodecahedron]], the great icosidodecahedron is not a [[stellation]] of the icosidodecahedron, but a [[faceting]] of it instead.

It also shares its [[edge arrangement]] with the [[great icosihemidodecahedron]] (having the triangle faces in common), and with the [[great dodecahemidodecahedron]] (having the pentagram faces in common).

[[File:Great stellated dodecahedron truncations.gif|thumb|right|240px|Animated truncation sequence from &lbrace;{{frac|5|2}}, 3} to {3, {{frac|5|2}}}]]

The [[Truncation (geometry)|truncated]] ''great stellated dodecahedron'' is a [[Degeneracy_(mathematics)#Convex_polyhedron|degenerate]] polyhedron, with 20 triangular faces from the truncated vertices, and 12 (hidden) pentagonal faces as truncations of the original pentagram faces, the latter forming a [[great dodecahedron]] inscribed within and sharing the edges of the icosahedron.

=== Great rhombic triacontahedron===
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|gID}}
[[File:Great rhombic triacontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great rhombic triacontahedron]]
The [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the great icosidodecahedron is the ''great rhombic triacontahedron''; it is nonconvex, [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] and [[isotoxal]].  It has 30 intersecting [[rhombus|rhombic]] faces. It can also be called the great stellated triacontahedron.

The great rhombic triacontahedron can be constructed by expanding the size of the faces of a [[rhombic triacontahedron]] by a factor of ''τ''<sup>3</sup> = 1+2''τ'' = 2+√5, where ''τ'' is the [[golden ratio]].
